summary: Rei Yoshimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Waseda University, where he also held a professorship attested in 1996.
Reiho Masunaga was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Kaiten Nukariya. He was attested as a teacher at Komazawa University in 1956.

Reiko Ohnuma specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at UC Berkeley and completed her PhD at the University of Michigan under Luis O. Gómez and Padmanabh S. Jaini. She held posts at Texas, Alabama, and Dartmouth.

Reimon Yuki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Daijo Tokiwa at the University of Tokyo (DLitt 1927). He served at the Eastern Cultural Institute, University of Tokyo's Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia, and Kyoto Women's University.

Reiner Wiehl was a philosopher who studied at the University of Nancy and Goethe University Frankfurt. He served as Professor of Philosophy at the University of Hamburg (1969–1977) and Heidelberg University (appointed 1977).
Reinhold Grünendahl is an Indologist who held posts at the Free University of Berlin (attested 1983) and the Göttingen State and University Library (attested 2008).

Reinhold Klotz was a scholar in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He completed his Habilitation at Leipzig University (1826–1831), where he served as assistant professor from 1832 and außerordentlicher Professor from 1849 to 1870.

Reinhold Niebuhr was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Elmhurst University, Eden Theological Seminary, and Yale Divinity School. He held a post at Union Theological Seminary from circa 1928 to 1960.

Reinhold Rost was a linguist and Indologist who earned his PhD from the University of Jena under Johann Gustav Stickel and Johann Gildemeister. He taught at St Augustine's College and served as Head Librarian at the India Office (1869–1893).
Reirin Yamada was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and later served as president of Komazawa Junior College.

Reita Nakamura is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies at Toyo University. In 2015, he was attested as a graduate student researcher at Toyo University and as a researcher at the Shinran Buddhist Center.
Remeen Firoz is a doctoral student in Indology and related studies at the Australian National University, working under supervisor Assa Doron (attested 2026).

Renate Syed is an Indologist who earned her doctorate at the University of Munich under Dieter Schlingloff, Friedrich Wilhelm, and Gritli von Mitterwallner. She was attested as a Privatdozentin at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2026.
Renjo Akamatsu was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Chō Sanshū and held a post at Ryukoku University.
René Gothóni is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Helsinki from circa 1971 to 1982 and held an academic post there from circa 1975 to 2014.

René Grousset worked in history, archaeology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and sinology after studying at the University of Montpellier. He held posts at the Musée Guimet, Musée Cernuschi, École du Louvre, Louvre Museum, and École Libre des Sciences Politiques.
René Guénon was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at the Robert-Badinter School Complex, Collège-lycée Jacques-Decour, and the University of Paris.

René de Nebesky-Wojkowitz was a Tibetologist and religious studies scholar. Educated at the University of Vienna, SOAS, Berlin, and LSE, he studied under Koppers, Haekel, Bleichsteiner, Tucci, and Rock, and served at Weltmuseum Wien in 1958.

Rewata Dhamma was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned degrees, including a PhD, from Sampurnanand Sanskrit University between 1956 and 1967, as well as a doctorate from Banaras Hindu University.

Richard A. Hutch is a religious studies scholar who studied at Gettysburg College, Yale Divinity School, and the University of Chicago. He held academic posts at Southern Illinois University Carbondale (~1974–1978) and the University of Queensland (~1978–2011).
